text:
Jesus Sanchez
Jan. 1, 1934 - Sept. 6, 2026
In Loving Memory of Jesus Sanchez
Jesus Sanchez, beloved husband, father, father-in-law, grandfather and friend, passed away peacefully on September 6, 2026, at the age of 92 surrounded by family.
Jesus was born on January 1, 1934, in Rancho La Granada, Mexico to a loving family of thirteen children. Growing up alongside his siblings, he learned the importance of family, hard work, responsibility, and looking out for one another at an early age. Those lessons stayed with him throughout his life and became the core values he instilled on to his daughter and granddaughter.
In 1962, Jesus and Sara, the love of his life, married and immigrated to the United States. They left behind their families, familiar places and people they knew, carrying with them hope for a better life and determination to build a future for themselves and their family.
They created a home outside of Holtville, California, where they lived for over 60 years. Together, they faced challenges of starting a new life in a new country, relying on their faith, love for one another, and willingness to work hard.
A man of strong Catholic faith, Jesus trusted in God throughout his life. He valued family, prayer, and the traditions of his Catholic faith and carried those beliefs with him throughout his journey. He found comfort in knowing that, after a life well lived, he would be welcomed home to eternal life with the Lord.
Jesus found his calling as a livestock foreman, a position that reflected his knowledge, dedication, leadership, and deep respect for animals. He took great pride in his work and understood the responsibility that came with caring for livestock. Whether tending animals, working cattle, supervising daily ranch operations, repairing fences, maintaining equipment, or helping those around him; Jesus brought years of knowledge and a strong work ethic to everything he did. He never shied away from a hard day’s work.
He earned the respect of those who worked alongside him and found satisfaction in a job well done. His years as a livestock foreman were more than a career—they were a reflection of the man he was: dependable, hardworking, humble, and committed to caring for the people and the animals entrusted to him.
Some of his greatest memories were made working around livestock and spending time with family. Everyone knew that they were always welcomed at his outdoor kitchen; he had a cup of coffee ready and will always offer you something to eat. He enjoyed sharing his knowledge and teaching his daughter, son-in-law, granddaughter, and family friends the value of hard work. He showed them that there is dignity in working with your hands, taking care of what has been entrusted to you, and finishing a job well.
Jesus was a devoted husband who shared his life's journey with Sara. Together, they built a home, raised their family, faced life's challenges, and celebrated its blessings. Their marriage was a lasting testament to their love, courage, faith, and determination.
He was also a loving father and grandfather who treasured his family above all else. His granddaughter held a particularly special place in his heart, and he loved watching her grow, sharing stories, and giving her memories that will remain with her for a lifetime.
He will be remembered for his strong work ethic, quiet strength, generous heart, and unwavering love for his family. His journey was one of courage, resilience, faith, and perseverance — a story that will remain an important part of his family's history.
Jesus is survived by his daughter Laura Sanchez Guerrero (Mo) of El Centro, CA, his granddaughter, Sara Jessica Scoggins (Lane) of Olsburg, KS, his sister, Margarita Espindula of Colima, MX and numerous friends.
He was preceded in death by his wife, Sara Sanchez, parents Jesus Sanchez Gonzalez and Elodia Cervantes Ramirez, and eleven siblings.
Services for Jesus Sanchez will be held on Friday, October 2, 2026, at St. Joseph’s Catholic Church in Holtville, CA. Visitation will be at 9:00 am, followed by the rosary at 9:30 am and mass at 10:00 am. Burial service will take place following the mass at Evergreen Cemetery in El Centro, CA. Services are under the direction of Hems Brothers Mortuary in El Centro, CA.
